question: A medical student asks you why donor breast milk in the human milk bank must be pasteurised before being given to preterm infants. Which statement BEST describes the Holder pasteurisation process and its trade-off?

answers.text: Milk is heated to 72°C for 15 seconds (HTST), which eliminates all pathogens and preserves all immunological components intact

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: HTST (High Temperature Short Time) at 72°C/15 seconds is used for commercial milk pasteurisation, NOT for human milk banks. It is not used for donor milk because it does not preserve bioactive components as well as Holder pasteurisation.

answers.text: Milk is heated to 62.5°C for 30 minutes (Holder pasteurisation), eliminating HIV and CMV while partially preserving secretory IgA, lactoferrin, and growth factors

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Holder pasteurisation (62.5°C for 30 minutes) is the international standard for donor human milk banks. It eliminates HIV, CMV, and bacterial pathogens. The trade-off is partial loss of bioactive components: secretory IgA is partially preserved, but lysozyme, lactoferrin, and cellular components are reduced.

answers.text: Milk is sterilised at 121°C for 15 minutes in an autoclave, ensuring complete pathogen elimination with preservation of all protein components

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Autoclaving at 121°C would denature all proteins and destroy all bioactive components in breast milk. This method is used for surgical equipment sterilisation, not human milk banking.

answers.text: Milk is UV-irradiated at 254 nm for 20 minutes, which inactivates viruses without any loss of nutritional or immunological components

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: UV irradiation is an experimental technique, not the standard for human milk banks. Holder pasteurisation (62.5°C/30 min) is the WHO-endorsed and internationally accepted standard method.

overallFeedback.feedback: The standard for human milk banks is Holder pasteurisation: 62.5°C for 30 minutes. It eliminates HIV and CMV but causes partial loss of bioactive components such as lysozyme, lactoferrin, and immune cells.

Excellent. Holder pasteurisation: 62.5°C for 30 minutes. It eliminates HIV, CMV, and other pathogens while partially preserving secretory IgA, lactoferrin, and growth factors — a deliberate trade-off between safety and bioactivity.
